messages.text:
I received this miner and it has worked fine until recently when I did the firmware update and it switched to a new OS and firmware and the Hashrate dropped to around 47 to 50 MH/s. Please let me know if you can assist. Thannk you.

See screenshot that is attached.

Stephen P.
Note to the team: I'll look at the screenshot first.
Handed to the team · Need JD's eyes on a post-update hashrate collapse; model, firmware version and t

Hi Stephen,

Thanks for writing in, and sorry the update left you worse off than before. I want to help you get the hashrate back where it belongs. One thing first: the screenshot did not come through on my side, so rather than guess at what it shows, could you resend it in your reply? A photo of the screen or a screenshot of the web dashboard is perfect.

Two details would let me pin this down quickly: the exact model of the unit, and the firmware version it is running now. On Harlo OS the version is shown in the Settings or System area of the web interface, and also on the device screen on most models. Once I have those two things plus the screenshot I can tell you whether what you are seeing is a real drop or a reporting problem.

In the meantime, here is what usually explains a collapse like this straight after an update. First, the firmware may simply be behind. Go to https://harlolabs.com/ and check the latest release for your exact model, then, if you are already on Harlo OS, use its Firmware updates section with the OTA image so your settings and Wi-Fi are kept. Second, an update very often resets the performance settings, so the ASIC frequency and core voltage fall back to a conservative default, and the unit then runs at a fraction of its rated speed even though everything looks healthy. Check the performance or mining preset in the interface and set it back to the normal or factory preset for your model rather than the lowest one. Third, give it time before judging: the hashrate figure is a rolling average, so right after a reboot it reads low for a while, and the pool side average needs roughly an hour of shares before it means anything. Fourth, check the temperatures and that the fan is spinning properly, because a hot chip will throttle itself down hard, and check that you are on the original power supply and a direct wall socket, since an underpowered or sagging supply makes the firmware drop the clock to stay stable.

If all of that is in order and it still sits around 47 to 50 MH/s, the next step is a clean full installation rather than an OTA. On https://harlolabs.com/ you can connect the miner by USB data cable and do the erase and install for your exact model. Be aware this wipes saved settings, Wi-Fi credentials and any pairing, so you will set up the pool and Wi-Fi again afterwards. It clears a bad partial flash, which is a common cause of a unit that runs but barely hashes.

I have also passed your case to JD, our hardware lead, with what we know so far. We are closed over the weekend, so he picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET and his answer comes straight to you by email. If you would like faster hands-on help in the meantime, our Discord is very active at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , in the Harlo OS channel, and you can mention @nullhashrate there, which is JD.

Send me the model, the firmware version and that screenshot and we will get to the bottom of it.

Hal
HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Handed to the team · DC06 running at roughly 15 percent of rated hashrate after a firmware move to NO

Hi Stephen,

Thanks, the screenshot came through this time and it tells me a lot. Your unit is a Hammer DC06, the scrypt Dogecoin and Litecoin miner, and it is rated at about 330 MH/s drawing roughly 105 watts. Your dashboard shows 47 to 59 MH/s at 66.9 watts, with the ASIC at 2300 MHz, input 12.1 volts, hashboard at 47.5 C, VRM at 64 C and the fan at 73 percent. So the power and the temperatures are healthy and the board is clearly alive, it is just delivering a fraction of the work it should for the power it is burning. With 18 hours of uptime and a dead flat line on the graph, this is not an averaging artefact either. Something in the new NORN OS build is either running the board on a crippled profile or losing most of the work the chips produce.

Here is what I would like you to do, in this order. First, open the Settings page and look for the mining or performance profile, sometimes shown as a preset such as eco, balanced or turbo, along with the frequency and voltage fields. A firmware jump very often resets those to a conservative default or to a profile that does not match the DC06 board. Set it back to the factory or default profile for the DC06, save, and use the RESTART button at the top right. Give it 20 minutes and see where the graph settles.

Second, open the Logs page and let it run for a few minutes. What I am looking for is the chip or ASIC count the firmware detects at startup, and whether you see hardware errors, rejected shares or repeated reconnects. If a slice of the chips is not being detected, the log will say so at boot, and that would explain both the low hashrate and the lower than normal power draw. A screenshot of the first 30 or so lines after a restart would be perfect.

Third, a pool note. You are on the unmineable scrypt endpoint on port 3333. The local figure on your dashboard is measured by the miner itself, so the pool is not the cause of what you are seeing, but once the unit is healthy again it is worth comparing the two, since a pool side number always lags and swings for the first hour. If after the profile reset the local number is still stuck around 50 MH/s, the next thing is the firmware itself rather than any setting. On the DC06 the fix for a bad or mismatched flash is a clean reinstall rather than another over the air update. If NORN OS offers you a full install or a rollback to the version you were on before, that is the one to take, and if you remember which version it was running before the update please tell me, since that is a strong clue on its own. Do not install any third party or unofficial image on it, that is the one route that can cost you the warranty. You can also check the model list on https://harlolabs.com/ to see whether the DC06 is supported there, since our own Harlo OS has fixed exactly this kind of post update hashrate loss on Hammer hardware.

I have also passed the full picture to JD, our hardware lead, so he can confirm whether this NORN OS 3.0.0 build is known to downclock the DC06 and what the correct image for your board version is. We are closed this evening, so he picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET and his answer comes to you right here by email. If you want faster hands on help in the meantime, our Discord is very active at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , and you can mention @nullhashrate there, which is JD.

Send me the Logs screenshot and what the profile settings say, and we will get this back to 330.

Hal
HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Thank you

Hi Stephen,

Thanks for pulling the log, that part is genuinely useful. The photo did not reach me on this one, so I am only going on the text you pasted rather than guessing at an image I cannot see. Could you attach the dashboard screenshot again in your reply, or just type out the hashrate figure and the firmware version now showing in the Overview panel.

What the log tells me is actually good news about one thing and bad news about another. The miner is ramping chain 0 cleanly in 50 MHz steps all the way up and finishing with frequency ramping completed successfully at 2300 MHz, with no chip errors along the way. That means the firmware is applying the full intended clock and the chain is accepting it. So this is not a conservative profile or a stuck low clock, which was my first suspicion. If the hashrate is still sitting around 50 MH/s while the chain runs at its full 2300 MHz, then the clock is right and the work simply is not coming back from part of the hashboard, and that is a different kind of problem.

Two things would settle it. First, tell me the hashrate reading now, after the new Hammer OS build, and the firmware version string in the Overview, so I know for certain the new image took. Second, send me the log lines from a bit earlier in the boot, the ones above the frequency ramp. That is where the firmware prints how many chips or cores it found on the chain, and comparing that number with what a healthy DC06 reports is the single fastest way to tell a firmware problem from a hardware one. If your Logs page lets you scroll to the top after a restart, the first 20 or 30 lines are exactly what I need.

While you are in there, it is also worth noting the rejected and hardware error counters if the dashboard shows them, and what the power draw reads now. Previously you were at 66.9 watts against roughly 105 watts for a healthy DC06, and that gap is consistent with part of the board not doing work.

JD has all of this, including the ramp log, so he can compare your chip count against a known good unit. He is back tomorrow at 10am ET and his reply comes to you in this thread. If you want a quicker look in the meantime, our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf is very active and you can mention @nullhashrate there, which is JD.

Send me those earlier boot lines and the current hashrate and we will know what we are dealing with.

Hal
HeliumDeploy Technical Support
